text.p: Hungarian share prices closed lower on Monday, belying dealers' expectations that the Budapest bourse could shake off the bearish trend.
The BUX index closed at 3,505.66 points, down 56.43.
Both pharmaceutical shares experienced further losses, with Richter closing at 7,950 forints, down 150, and Egis finishing at 7,900, down 200, in high turnover.
"There were some large deals in both pharmaceutical shares," said Gyorgy Czipo of ING Barings.
The two pharmaceuticals shares accounted for 1.16 billion forints of the relatively large total spot share turnover of 1.7 billion forints.
Dealers did not venture to predict when the present bearish trend would turn around, but dropping BUX index futures indicate little optimism.
All six BUX index futures dropped by between 25 to 55 points. The June maturity finished at 4,030 points, down 55.
"Foreign investors' profit-taking seems to continue," Czipo said, adding that the growing number of buyers on Monday was more than compensated by sellers.
"In early trade, some dealers must have thought that it is worth buying at current prices. Later on, prices dropped further and they lost confidence," Czipo said.
Retail group Fotex and financial consultant Dunaholding published their January-September results on Monday.
Fotex closed at 94 forints, down 2, while Dunaholding put on 50 points to end at 7,950 forints.
